questions.question: What happens to net exports when foreign income rises?
questions.explanation: The source states that net exports rise as the income of the rest of the world goes up (Q0003).

evidence.quote:
So net exports is increasing in the income
 of the rest of the world.

questions.topic: foreign income effect on net exports

original_segments.text: But it's not so.
First, because we have another income that matters here,
which is the income of the rest of the world,
but more important because we also have an exchange.
But let's start from this side.
So net exports is increasing in the income
of the rest of the world.
Why is that?
That is demand for domestically produced goods
rises when foreign income goes up.
for an output for an income goes up.
Why is that?
It's a symmetric argument, no?
If with imports, well, our exports
are the imports of the other country.
So if the income in the other country goes up,
then their imports will go up, which
is our exports that go up.
That's the reason that exports goes up.
And the last term, remember, says
that net exports is declining on the real exchange rate. Why is that? What happens when
the real exchange rate goes up? It makes our goods more expensive relative to foreign goods.

questions.question: Why does higher foreign income lead to higher net exports?
questions.answer: Because foreign consumers demand more domestically produced goods.
questions.explanation: The source explains that demand for domestically produced goods rises when foreign income goes up (Q0005).

questions.explanation: The source says a higher real exchange rate makes domestic goods more expensive relative to foreign goods, lowering net exports (Q0015).

questions.question: If a foreign country's income rises, what happens to its imports from the domestic country?
questions.answer: The foreign country's imports increase, which are the domestic country's exports.
questions.explanation: The source notes that when foreign income goes up, their imports (which are the domestic country's exports) go up (Q0010).
